notesStmt.note: The note on this manuscript was made sometime after the poem's publication, likely sometime in early 1889.

An uncorrected proof slip of the poem "To the Year 1889," first published in the Critic on January 5, 1889. The slip contains a note in Whitman's hand. The poem was later included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891) under the title "To the Pending Year."

lg.l:
Have I no weapon-word for thee—some message brief and
fierce?

Have I fought out and done indeed the battle? Is there no
shot left,
For all thy affectations, lisps, scorns, manifold silliness?
Nor for myself—my own rebellious self in thee?
Down, down, proud gorge!—though choking thee;
Thy bearded throat and high-borne forehead to the gutter;
Crouch low thy neck eleemosynary gifts.
